verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. The displayed identity is reproduced term for term: −R_b = −pulseRatio; (D + c_η)m = ((1/2 − h) + (1/2 − h)·η·shapeGradient η)·normalizedLag, with m the exact lag, not its expansion; −Dηm_η = −(1/2 − h)·η·∂_η(normalizedLag). Two ways the Lean is stronger, neither a weakening. First, `Ns_pulse_identity` is an exact equality with an explicit named remainder `axialHistoryError`, not an O(·). Second, that remainder is bounded by axialErrorConstant(P,m)·λ^29, whereas the paper writes O(C_pre λ^27); since λ ≤ 1/120 here, C_pre λ^29 ≤ C_pre λ^27, so the Lean bound implies the paper's and is tighter by two powers. The hypotheses attached to the bound (wait = 60 log(1/λ), λ ≤ 1/120, |amp η| ≤ 6/5, |amp'η| ≤ 1, |η| ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ pulseLength) are the standing setting of Section A.5.
